claim: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && so only team OWNERs pass; team ADMINs (who are not the organizer/attendee) get FORBIDDEN.
body:
## [ISSUE] Team admin check uses `&&`, so team admins are rejected

**Severity:** HIGH -- team ADMINs cannot add guests to team bookings, contrary to the variable name and intent.

### The Problem
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
`isTeamAdmin` (`packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264`) matches memberships with role `ADMIN` **or** `OWNER`; `isTeamOwner` (`:286`) matches only `OWNER`. `admin && owner` reduces to `owner`, so an ADMIN membership evaluates to `false`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
A team admin opening a teammate's booking gets `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission`. Only owners pass. The variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` shows the intent was OR.

### Research
`isTeamAdmin` already includes OWNER, so a second call is unnecessary. Elsewhere (e.g. `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner` used in `BookingListItem.tsx`) admin-or-owner is a single check.

### Recommendation
```ts
const teamId = booking.eventType?.teamId;
const isTeamAdminOrOwner = teamId ? !!(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) : false;
```
This also avoids two DB queries against `teamId = 0` for non-team bookings.

claim: The handler authorises any attendee (matched by email) and never checks booking status/time, so attendees and callers of the API can add guests to cancelled/past/rejected bookings and trigger emails, unlike editLocation which is restricted to organizer/collective hosts.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Authorization is broader than sibling mutations and there is no booking-status guard

**Severity:** MEDIUM -- lets non-hosts send organizer-branded emails and mutate cancelled/past bookings.

### The Problem
```ts
const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN
```
Any logged-in user whose email is on the attendee list may add arbitrary guests. There is also no check of `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`.

### Theory / Proof
- The sibling `editLocation` mutation uses `bookingsProcedure` (`bookings/util.ts:19-46`), which only loads the booking when `userId === ctx.user.id` or the user is a host on a COLLECTIVE event type. `addGuests` uses a plain `authedProcedure` with its own, looser check.
- The UI only offers the action for upcoming, non-cancelled bookings (`BookingListItem.tsx:544` `isUpcoming && !isCancelled`), but the tRPC endpoint is callable directly.
- For each new guest the handler sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` with `from: organizer.name`, i.e. an attendee can make Cal.com send confirmation emails in the organizer's name to any address.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Calling `viewer.bookings.addGuests` on a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking inserts attendees and sends "scheduled" confirmations with an ICS for a meeting that no longer exists.

### Recommendation
Reject non-active bookings and consider whether attendees should have this ability at all:
```ts
if (booking.status === BookingStatus.CANCELLED || booking.status === BookingStatus.REJECTED || dayjs(booking.endTime).isBefore(dayjs()))
  throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "booking_not_editable" });
```

claim: Blacklist and duplicate filtering compare raw guest strings case-sensitively (and without extractBaseEmail), so 'Blocked@x.com' or 'blocked+1@x.com' bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and existing attendees can be re-added with different casing.

sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee included in the request is filtered from the insert but still receives a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' email.
body:
## [ISSUE] Emails are keyed off unfiltered `guests`, not `uniqueGuests`

**Severity:** MEDIUM -- existing attendees can get a duplicate booking confirmation.

### The Problem
```ts
await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);
```
`uniqueGuests` (line 74) filtered out addresses already on the booking, but `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`email-manager.ts:525`) uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide between `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new booking confirmation) and `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Request `guests: ["existing@x.com", "new@x.com"]`: only `new@x.com` is inserted, but `existing@x.com` is in `guests`, so they receive a full "scheduled" confirmation email again rather than the "guests added" notice.

### Recommendation
```ts
await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, uniqueGuests);
```

claim: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, unlike sendLocationChangeEmails and other senders, so hosts/attendees get Cal.com emails even when the event type disables them.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not respect `disableStandardEmails`

**Severity:** MEDIUM -- violates a per-event-type setting that other senders honour.

### The Problem
```ts
export const sendAddGuestsEmails = async (calEvent: CalendarEvent, newGuests: string[]) => {
  ...
  emailsToSend.push(sendEmail(() => new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent: calendarEvent })));
```
There is no `eventTypeMetadata` parameter and no `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` guard.

### Theory / Proof
The immediately preceding sibling `sendLocationChangeEmails` (`email-manager.ts:495-523`) takes `eventTypeMetadata` and wraps host emails in `if (!eventTypeDisableHostEmail(...))` and attendee emails in `if (!eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(...))`. Event types that set `metadata.disableStandardEmails` (e.g. those using custom workflows) expect Cal.com to send none of the standard emails.

### Recommendation
```ts
export const sendAddGuestsEmails = async (calEvent: CalendarEvent, newGuests: string[], eventTypeMetadata?: EventTypeMetadata) => {
  if (!eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)) { /* organizer + team members */ }
  if (!eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)) { /* attendees */ }
```
and call it with `booking.eventType?.metadata as EventTypeMetadata` from the handler.

claim: The server schema accepts an unbounded array with duplicates; uniqueness is only enforced client-side, so duplicate emails create duplicate attendee rows and a single request can email an arbitrary number of addresses.
body:
## [ISSUE] Server schema has no uniqueness or size limit on `guests`

**Severity:** MEDIUM -- duplicate attendee rows and an unbounded email fan-out per request.

### The Problem
```ts
guests: z.array(z.string().email()),
```
Uniqueness is only checked in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` via a client-side `refine`. The handler's `uniqueGuests` filter only removes addresses already on the booking, not duplicates within the request.

### What happens today vs. what will break
`{ bookingId, guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] }` sent directly to the endpoint inserts two `Attendee` rows via `createMany` (no unique constraint on `(bookingId, email)`), and both appear in the calendar event and the emails. There is also no `.max()`, so one call can trigger an email to thousands of addresses.

### Recommendation
```ts
guests: z
  .array(z.string().email().transform((e) => e.toLowerCase()))
  .min(1)
  .max(10)
  .refine((g) => new Set(g).size === g.length, { message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" }),
```

claim: For seated event types the handler inserts attendees without BookingSeat rows and without checking seatsPerTimeSlot, so guests can exceed the seat limit and have no seat reference to cancel/reschedule.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Adding guests to seated bookings bypasses seat bookkeeping

**Severity:** MEDIUM -- seat capacity and per-seat operations become inconsistent.

### The Problem
```ts
data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails } } }
```
The handler reads `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` only to put it on `evt`; it never checks remaining capacity and never creates `BookingSeat` rows.

### Theory / Proof
Seat bookings are created in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/create/createNewSeat.ts`, which checks capacity against `seatsPerTimeSlot` and creates a `BookingSeat` (`seatsReferences`) for each attendee; cancellation/rescheduling of an individual seat depends on that reference. Attendees added here have none.

### What happens today vs. what will break
On an event with `seatsPerTimeSlot = 5` and 5 booked seats, the organizer or an attendee can add more guests, so the slot holds more attendees than allowed, and the new guests cannot manage their own seat.

### Recommendation
Reject the operation for seated events, or route through the seat logic:
```ts
if (booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot)
  throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "cannot_add_guests_to_seated_event" });
```
